Fig. 3. Re-certification analysis (α=0.10). (a) Precision at a fixed 25-case budget, HB vs. WSR. (b) False-positive cost vs. in-domain calibration cases.
Fig. 2. Transfer audit (α=0.10). Per-organ FNR for AMOS in-distribution vs. frozenthreshold transfer to RAOS, with 95% CIs; highlighted organs exceed α on RAOS.

Table 2. Within high-probability control, WSR needs fewer cases than HB. Left: usable local RAOS budgets for the six Tier-1 organs; ranges span organs. A usable threshold controls held-out FNR and has precision ≥0.5; “simult.” uses Bonferroni δ/12 over all 12 at α=0.10. HB and WSR provide high-probability control; CRC provides expectation control, so their counts are not equivalent. Right: held-out case loss at n=25, α=0.10. Each column reports the worst statistic among organs with a nonvacuous threshold (CRC 9, WSR 6, HB 2); columns can refer to different organs. At α=0.05, HB never certifies the right kidney within our grid.

Table 1. Frozen AMOS thresholds λk and realized voxel FNR at α=0.10 on AMOS and the clinically shifted RAOS cohort, with 95% CI. Boldface marks RAOS FNR exceeding α; both adrenals’ λk=0.000 is vacuous; nAMOS/nRAOS are present-organ case counts.
